items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] David Meeker's, 'Jazz in the Movies - A Guide to Jazz Musicians, 1917 to 1977.'

ctx.x: The sound track I'd like to see out in records, though, because I was very happy with that.

Sounds like it would be great. As long as we're on films, may as well go through the book here. David Meeker's, "Jazz in the Movies - A Guide to Jazz Musicians, 1917 to 1977." And these are not chronological, but rather alphabetical. And the first one where you're listed is "Andy's Boogie," 1950, three minutes, Charlie Barnet and his Orchestra in a performance of the title number with the leader soloing on soprano sax. A Snader Telescription. Do you remember that?
That's very interesting, because I recall the arrangement very well, "Andy's Boogie," and I don't play soprano sax on it.
